question: If the body of an animal can be divided into two indistinguishable left and right halves through only one plane, then it possesses:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**bilateral symmetry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bilateral symmetry** refers to a body structure where an organism can be divided into two identical halves along a single plane.
 
• It is a common feature observed in animals belonging to the **phylum Chordata**, which includes mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
 
• This type of symmetry facilitates **directional movement**, as organisms with bilateral symmetry tend to have a distinct head (anterior) and tail (posterior) region.
 
• Examples of organisms with bilateral symmetry include **humans, dogs, cats, insects, and birds**.
 
• Bilateral symmetry is crucial for the development of complex body structures, including **sensory organs** and the **central nervous system**.
 
• This symmetry type is advantageous for the evolution of organisms that exhibit active locomotion and show specialization in body regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centre of symmetry**__

 __
 
• This term is not applicable to biological classifications. It is more commonly used in **geometry and crystallography** to describe a point in a figure or structure where symmetrical elements converge.
 
 
 
• **Asymmetricity**__
 __
 
• Asymmetricity refers to the absence of any symmetry in an organism. Examples include **sponges (Porifera)**, which do not exhibit a defined body plan or symmetry.
 
• Such organisms often rely on a simple structure for functions like feeding and reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Radial symmetry**__
 
 
• Radial symmetry is observed in organisms whose body parts are arranged around a central axis, allowing multiple planes to divide the body into identical halves.
 
• Examples include **cnidarians (jellyfish, corals)** and **echinoderms (starfish, sea urchins)**.
 
• This type of symmetry is well-suited for animals that interact with the environment equally in all directions.
